learning: If steering_oscillation on the oval stays near 0.2 and slalom progress rises above 0.25, keep y=0.08 m. If oscillation rises sharply, the extra lookahead is adding lag, so return to y=0.07 m and add kd in small steps.
notes: Iteration 3 controller and array layout kept; only sensor y moves from 0.07 to 0.08 m, matching the Builder's proposal. Tests whether extra lookahead improves slalom and s-bend without raising oval oscillation.
rationale: The Builder's proposal moves the 5-sensor row from y=0.07 to y=0.08 m and keeps the iteration 3 drivetrain (wheel_track 0.09, wheel_radius 0.035, mass 0.6) and array layout (x = -0.03 to +0.03 m, 0.015 m pitch, 0.012 m footprint). I kept the iteration 3 controller unchanged (base_speed 1.7, kp 2.5, ki 0.05, kd 0.4, weights -2 to +2, last_direction line loss). Iteration 3 scored 328.4 with oval rms_error 0.0146 and steering_oscillation 0.18, and its s-bend progress (0.446) was the best yet. Its slalom progress stayed at 0.17 and max_error stayed near the 0.06 m off-track limit, so the controller is not the bottleneck there. Changing the sensor row alone isolates the lookahead effect. Iteration 2 showed that a wider, heavier sensor span adds oscillation, so I do not widen the array. I did not raise kd to offset the extra lag, because that would confound the test. The main risk is oscillation rising on the oval; if it does, the next step is to return to y=0.07 m or add kd.
